title: Recommended for award without the lowest price
question: How often is the firm put forward for award not the cheapest on the bid sheet, and what is the difference?
finding: On 16 of 86 lists with a recommendation the firm put forward was not the lowest tabulated price, a difference of $12.3 million in total. On 3 the lowest bidder asked to withdraw its bid after opening ($8.8 million more to the next firm); on 7 the gap sits inside the local-business bid discount ($1.6 million).
how: The firm named after "award to" in the same agenda item, compared with the lowest total price on the tabulation. The reason shown is read from the staff report in the same file where it gives one.
limits: The sample is small: 108 bid lists (71 Public Works 2022–26, 15 Port, 22 Muni), only contracts large enough to go to a commission with the tabulation attached. The airport and the water department publish none without a login. There are routine reasons: City law gives certified local businesses a bid discount of up to 10% for ranking, State law lets a bidder withdraw a bid that contains a clerical mistake, low bids are thrown out as non-responsive, and some awards are on the base bid without alternates. It is also the step a reader would want explained when the next price is much higher. Whether the commission adopted each recommendation was not checked.
